skill.name: comprehensive-code-review
skill.description: Guides an AI assistant through a rigorous multi-pass review of pull requests and local code changes, with GitHub PR posting support.
skill.summary: Run structured, critical code reviews for pull requests and changed code.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code references, Mermaid diagrams, and safe shell snippets. No prompt injection attempt was found, but the skill repeatedly requires posting reviews to GitHub and can create blocking PR review actions. Those external publication and workflow-state behaviors need user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Mandatory GitHub posting can publish review details without clear consent.
remediation.suggestion: Change the skill to ask for explicit confirmation before posting comments or reviews to GitHub. Support a local-only review mode.

remediation.issue: Blocking request-changes reviews can alter pull request workflow state.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit user approval step before running gh pr review --request-changes or gh pr review --approve.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI command examples use placeholder PR identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to validate PR numbers as numeric values before passing them to shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory GitHub Publication Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires every review to be posted as a GitHub PR comment and treats local-only reviews as failed. This can expose review details to GitHub when a user expected local analysis.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mandatory posting requirement is repeated in multiple sections and includes a concrete gh pr comment command. The risk depends on user consent and repository visibility, but the publication intent is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Blocking Pull Request State Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to use a blocking request-changes review when coverage checks fail. This can alter PR workflow state and should require explicit user authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly name gh pr review --request-changes and define approval rules that force blocking reviews. This is expected for code review, but it is still an external state change.

high_findings.title: Mandatory GitHub Publication Without Confirmation
high_findings.description: The skill requires every review to be posted as a GitHub PR comment and treats local-only reviews as failed. This can expose review details to GitHub when a user expected local analysis.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mandatory posting requirement is repeated in multiple sections and includes a concrete gh pr comment command. The risk depends on user consent and repository visibility, but the publication intent is explicit.

medium_findings.title: Blocking Pull Request State Changes
medium_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to use a blocking request-changes review when coverage checks fail. This can alter PR workflow state and should require explicit user authorization.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly name gh pr review --request-changes and define approval rules that force blocking reviews. This is expected for code review, but it is still an external state change.

content.value_statement: Code changes can hide runtime failures, missing requirements, and weak verification plans. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured review before merge.
actual_capabilities: Guides a six-pass review covering change explanation, defects, consistency, architecture, compatibility, verification, and context synthesis.
Supports parallel reviewer mode with multiple independent reviews and a synthesized final report.
Checks issue links and requirement coverage before approval decisions.
Generates structured review sections with findings, simplifications, questions, checks, and task summaries.
Provides GitHub CLI workflows for reading PR context and posting PR comments or reviews.
Encourages Mermaid diagrams to explain data flow, dependencies, and system impact.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access for PR posting workflows.
Can be too strict for quick exploratory reviews.
Depends on available PR, issue, diff, and repository context.
Does not replace maintainer judgment or project-specific review policy.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review a pull request for missing requirements, runtime failures, and verification gaps before merging.

use_cases.title: Agent Work Quality Check
use_cases.description: Audit changes produced by another AI agent before asking a human reviewer to approve them.

use_cases.title: Critical Feature Review
use_cases.description: Run parallel reviewers and synthesize findings for risky changes that need higher confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current local changes with the comprehensive code review skill. Focus on runtime failures, missing tests, and clear fix suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR #123 using the six-pass process. Include change explanation, required fixes, possible simplifications, questions, suggested checks, and task summary.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Issue Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PR against its linked issue. Build a requirement checklist, cite evidence for each item, and request changes for any missing work.

prompt_templates.title: Run Parallel Review Synthesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Run code-review-3 for this PR. Launch three independent reviews, compare convergent and divergent findings, then synthesize one prioritized review.

output_examples.input: Review a feature PR that adds retry logic to an API handler.
output_examples.output: The review explains changed files, shows retry flow, flags missing timeout tests, suggests a shared retry helper, and lists exact verification commands.

output_examples.input: Check whether a PR fully implements its linked issue.
output_examples.output: The review lists every requirement, marks implemented and missing items, cites file evidence, and requests changes for incomplete coverage.

output_examples.input: Run three reviewers on a risky payment workflow change.
output_examples.output: The synthesis groups findings found by multiple reviewers, separates unique concerns, and produces a prioritized action list for the PR author.

best_practices: Provide the PR number, linked issue, and any acceptance criteria before starting the review.
Run build and test commands first, then ask the skill to focus on remaining risks.
Confirm before posting comments or blocking reviews to GitHub.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for lightweight style-only reviews where strict gates are unnecessary.
Posting review comments to GitHub before the author approves publication.
Treating the generated review as final without maintainer judgment.

faq.question: Does this skill only work with GitHub?
faq.answer: It is designed around GitHub PR workflows and the GitHub CLI. Local diff review is also described.

faq.question: Can it review uncommitted changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes local git diff workflows when no pull request is available.

faq.question: What makes parallel review mode different?
faq.answer: It asks multiple independent reviewers to inspect the same changes, then combines convergent and unique findings.

faq.question: Does it automatically approve pull requests?
faq.answer: It includes approval and request-changes commands, but users should require confirmation before changing PR state.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a security review skill?
faq.answer: It can flag security risks during code review, but it is broader than a dedicated security audit.
